chapterMaps.narrative: Moses gathers all Israel in Moab for a covenant beyond the one at Horeb. He recalls Egypt and forty years when their clothes did not wear out. Everyone stands before the LORD: leaders, men, children, wives, and foreigners. Even the woodcutter and the water carrier are there. The covenant is also made with those not present that day. No one who turns to other gods in secret will be pardoned. Later nations will ask why the land was ruined and hear the reason. Secret things belong to the LORD, and revealed things to Israel and its children.

chapterMaps.narrative: When scattered Israel returns to the LORD, he will gather them. He will bring them back from the farthest places. He will change their hearts so they love him and live. The command is not too hard or too far away. It is not in heaven or across the sea. The word is very near, in their mouth and heart. Moses sets life and death, blessing and curse, before them. He tells them to choose life by loving the LORD and holding to him.

chapterMaps.narrative: Moses is 120 and tells Israel he will not cross the Jordan. The LORD and Joshua will go before them, so they must be strong. Moses writes the law and gives it to the priests and elders. Every seven years, at the feast of booths, it must be read to everyone. Men, women, children, and foreigners are to hear and learn. The LORD tells Moses the people will turn to other gods after his death. Moses writes a song to stand as a witness against them. The book of the law is placed beside the ark.

chapterMaps.narrative: Moses sings a song and calls heaven and earth to listen. He calls God the Rock, whose work is perfect and whose ways are just. God found Israel in a desert and carried it as an eagle does. He fed Israel with honey and oil from the rock. But Israel grew fat, kicked, and left the God who made it. It turned to strange gods, so God hid his face. Yet he will judge his people and have compassion when their strength is gone. The LORD then tells Moses to climb Mount Nebo, see the land, and die there.

chapterMaps.narrative: Before he dies, Moses blesses the tribes of Israel. He says the LORD came from Sinai and loves the people. Moses gave them a law as the inheritance of all Jacob. He asks that Reuben live and that the LORD hear Judah. Levi keeps the Urim and Thummim and teaches the law. Benjamin rests in safety, and Joseph’s land is blessed with dew and deep water. Zebulun, Issachar, Gad, Dan, Naphtali, and Asher each get a saying. Moses ends: no one is like God, and Israel is saved by the LORD.

chapterMaps.narrative: Moses climbs Mount Nebo, and the LORD shows him the whole land. The LORD says this is the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moses may see it but not cross over. Moses dies there in Moab, and no one knows his tomb. He was 120, with clear eyes and full strength. Israel weeps for him thirty days. Joshua is full of the spirit of wisdom, because Moses laid hands on him. No prophet like Moses has risen since, whom the LORD knew face to face.

textRoutes.title: Moses recalls the failed entry
textRoutes.summary: Moses speaks to all Israel east of the Jordan in the fortieth year. He recalls how the LORD told them at Horeb to go and take the land. He recalls choosing leaders and judges to share his load. At Kadesh the people asked for spies, who brought back good fruit. Still the people refused to go up and said the LORD hated them. The LORD swore that generation would not see the land, except Caleb and Joshua. Moses says the LORD was angry with him too. The people then went up without the LORD and were beaten back.
textRoutes.detail: Moses is speaking to the children of the people who refused at Kadesh. He says “you” throughout, as if they had been there (verses 26–27). The parents’ choice is told as the family’s own history. In verse 37 he adds his own loss: he also will not enter. He says it was “for your sakes,” tying his fate to theirs. Numbers 20:12 gives the reason as Moses’s own act at the rock. So the speech keeps the cost of the past in front of a new generation.
